name: ExZalted Freight Tracking & Quotes
author: johnpmandawe

sections.description:
ExZalted Freight Tracking gives freight forwarders, couriers, 3PLs and trucking companies a lightweight way to answer “where is my shipment?” and “how much will it cost?” from their WordPress site. Customers can track a shipment, request a quote, or sign in to see everything linked to their account, while your team manages it all from one place.

Features

Shipment tracking

  • Create and manage shipments: tracking number (or auto-generated), status, service, origin, destination, ETA, customer name and email, a public note and a private internal note
  • A history of tracking events per shipment (time, location and note), added automatically whenever the status changes
  • Your own status workflow: define the statuses you use (Pending, Picked up, In transit, At customs, Out for delivery, Delivered, Exception, or anything else)
  • Public tracking form with a clean status timeline
  • Optional “require email to view” protection on the public tracking form
  • Searchable, sortable, filterable shipments list with status counts
  • Import shipments from CSV (create and update in bulk, up to 2,000 rows per file) and export them to CSV
  • Download Template button on the import page: a ready-to-fill CSV with two example rows that use your own current statuses and services
  • Safe partial updates: columns missing from your file are left untouched on existing shipments, unusable values (unknown status, bad email or date) are ignored and reported, and semicolon or tab separated files from other locales are detected automatically
  • Tracking results are never cached, and only public information is shown (never the customer’s details or your internal notes)

Freight quote requests

  • Accessible multi-step quote form that also works without JavaScript
  • Built-in fields: service, pickup and delivery location, ready date, cargo type, pieces, weight, dimensions, special handling, notes, contact details and a consent checkbox
  • Conditional fields: for example, special handling details appear only for dangerous or perishable cargo
  • Optional instant estimate (base price + price per kg for each service), followed by a request for a final quote, with an editable disclaimer
  • Logged-in customers have their name and email pre-filled
  • Lead inbox with statuses (New, Quoted, Won, Lost), a quoted amount, internal notes, search and filters
  • CSV export that adapts to your form: one column for every field the form has right now, including custom fields, plus any removed field that still has stored answers
  • Confirmation email to the customer and an alert to your team, with the customer set as Reply-To
  • Quote validity period, with expired quotes clearly refused

From quote to shipment

  • Set a quote to Quoted and the customer is emailed the final price automatically, with a secure link to accept or decline it (no login needed)
  • The link opens your Customer portal page. Declining sets the quote to Lost and records the customer’s reason. Accepting sets it to Won and creates a linked shipment automatically
  • The customer then receives the tracking number by email, or your payment instructions
  • Optional “Wait for payment” mode: the shipment starts as Awaiting payment, and the customer gets the tracking number when you click Confirm payment received
  • Quotes can expire after a number of days you choose. Links are long random keys, stored only as a hash, rate limited and never indexed by search engines
  • Resend the price email at any time with a fresh link, or create a shipment from a quote by hand when the customer accepted by phone
  • Quote, shipment and customer response are linked, so you can jump between them in the admin

Customer portal

  • Customers sign in with a normal WordPress account and see only their own records: “My shipments” (with the full status timeline for each) and “My quote requests” (with status and quoted amount)
  • Records are matched by email address: a shipment whose customer email equals the account email, and quote requests submitted with it
  • Built-in login form with lost-password and registration links. After signing in on the portal page, customers return to the portal, even when WooCommerce or another plugin would normally send them to “My account”
  • Mobile-friendly tables and pagination

Branding and emails

  • Theme color setting: one color restyles the quote form, tracking form and customer portal, and text on buttons switches between light and dark automatically for readability
  • Per-page color override: a color shortcode attribute, or the Color panel in the block sidebar
  • Sender name and sender email: send the plugin’s emails from your own company address instead of the WordPress default
  • Customer replies go to your company: customer-facing emails set Reply-To to your sender email (or notification email, or site admin email), and alerts to your team set Reply-To to the customer
  • Editable email templates for status updates, quote confirmations, quote prices and quote acceptances, with placeholders such as {tracking_number}, {status}, {tracking_url} and {portal_url}
  • Plain-text emails that work with any SMTP plugin

Built for trust and compliance

  • No external services, no tracking, no cookies, nothing sent to the plugin author or any third party (the only messages that leave your site are the emails you configure, sent through your own mail setup)
  • Honeypot and per-visitor rate limiting against spam, and generic “not found” messages so tracking numbers cannot be guessed
  • Consent checkbox on the quote form
  • Works with the WordPress personal data export and erase tools, and adds suggested text to the privacy policy guide
  • Translation-ready, right-to-left friendly styles, accessible markup
  • Optional removal of all data when the plugin is deleted

For developers

  • The quote form is data-driven, and estimates run through a replaceable engine, so add-ons can extend both (see the FAQ for hooks)

How it works

  1. You add the tracking form, the quote form and the customer portal to pages, using blocks or shortcodes, and select the portal page in Settings.
  2. A customer requests a quote. The request lands in your lead inbox with the status New, and the customer and your team are emailed.
  3. You enter the quoted amount and set the status to Quoted. The customer is emailed the price with a secure accept/decline link.
  4. The customer opens the link and accepts or declines. Declining sets the quote to Lost. Accepting sets it to Won and creates a linked shipment.
  5. The customer receives the tracking number by email. If you turned on Wait for payment, they receive your payment instructions first, and you click Confirm payment received to start the shipment and send the tracking number.
  6. You update the shipment status as it moves. Each change is added to its timeline, and the customer can be emailed.
  7. Customers follow progress on the tracking page, or sign in to the portal to see all their shipments and quotes.

You can also create shipments by hand or import them from a CSV file at any time.

Shortcodes and blocks

Every shortcode also exists as a block in the block editor under the Widgets category.

  • [consignly_tracking] (block: Shipment Tracking): the public tracking form.
  • [consignly_quote_form] (block: Freight Quote Form): the multi-step quote request form.
  • [consignly_portal] (block: Customer Portal): the customer account area.

Optional: the color attribute overrides the theme color for that one instance, for example [consignly_quote_form color="#e8590c"]. In the block editor, use the Color panel in the block sidebar instead.

These instructions are also shown at the top of Freight Tracking → Settings.

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service. It makes no requests to the plugin author or to any third party, loads no remote scripts, fonts or images, and sends no usage data.

The plugin does send emails: confirmations, quote prices and shipment status updates go to the customer, and alerts go to your team. They are sent through your site’s normal wp_mail() configuration (your host or your SMTP plugin) and only to the addresses involved in a quote or shipment. If your mail setup uses an external email service, that service handles those emails under its own terms. The plugin itself never sends them anywhere else.

Privacy

Quote requests store the name, company, email, phone and shipment details entered by the visitor, plus any additional form answers. Quotes also store the price, the customer’s accept or decline answer with its optional reason, and a one-way hash of the secure link key (never the key itself). Shipments may store a customer name and email. A salted hash of the visitor IP is kept in a short-lived transient for rate limiting only. No cookies are set and no data is sent to the plugin author or any third party. The only messages that leave your site are the emails described above, sent through your own mail configuration. Logged-in customers can only see records that carry their own account email address. The plugin adds suggested text to the WordPress privacy policy guide and supports the personal data export and erase tools.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin and activate it.
  2. Go to Freight Tracking → Settings. Pick your theme color, review the statuses and services, and set the sender name and email.
  3. Create a page with the Shipment Tracking block (or [consignly_tracking]) and select it as the Tracking page in Settings.
  4. Create a page with the Freight Quote Form block (or [consignly_quote_form]).
  5. Create a page with the Customer Portal block (or [consignly_portal]) and select it as the Customer portal page in Settings. This is required if you send quote prices: the accept or decline link in the price email opens this page. It is only optional if you never email quote prices and do not want a customer account area.
  6. Add shipments under Freight Tracking → Shipments, or import them from a CSV file.
sections.faq:
Does it need WooCommerce?

No. The plugin is standalone.

Does it contact any external service?

No. The plugin sends emails (quote confirmations, quote prices, shipment updates and team alerts) through your site’s normal wp_mail() configuration, so those emails travel through your mail provider or SMTP plugin. Nothing else is sent, and nothing is sent to the plugin author or any third party.

Customers are sent to the WooCommerce My account page after logging in.

Not from the portal. When someone logs in from the plugin’s portal page, they come back to the portal. Logging in from any other form still follows your site’s normal rules.

How does a quote become a shipment?

Enter the quoted amount, set the status to Quoted and save: the customer is emailed the price with a secure link. When they accept, the quote becomes Won and a shipment is created and linked to it automatically. If they decline, the quote becomes Lost. See “How it works” above, or the guide at the top of Freight Tracking → Settings.

The customer has no account. Can they still accept a quote?

Yes. The link in the email contains a secret key, so no login is needed. Customers who do have an account can also respond from “My quote requests” in the portal.

What does “Wait for payment” do?

When on, an accepted quote creates a shipment with the status Awaiting payment. The customer is shown your payment instructions instead of a tracking number. After you check the payment, open the shipment and click Confirm payment received: the shipment moves to your first status and the customer is emailed the tracking number. When off, the shipment starts straight away.

The price email has no link.

The link opens on your Customer portal page, so select that page under Freight Tracking → Settings → Pages & access. Then use Resend price email on the quote.

Can customers upload proof of payment?

Not in the free plugin. Add-ons can add it with the consignly_quote_response_extra action, which prints on the accepted-quote page, and the consignly_payment_confirmed action.

Does the customer have a portal?

Yes. Add the Customer Portal block or [consignly_portal] to a page. Customers log in with a WordPress account and see the shipments whose customer email matches their account email, plus the quote requests they submitted with it. They never need to enter a tracking number or email there.

What does “Require the customer email to view a shipment” do?

It applies to the public tracking form only. The visitor must enter the same email address that is stored on the shipment, in addition to the tracking number. Customers using the portal are already signed in, so they are not asked for it.

How do customers get a portal account?

Create users yourself, or turn on public registration under Settings → General in WordPress. Because records are matched by email, keep the default registration flow, where the customer sets their password through a link emailed to them, so the address is verified.

How do I change the colors?

Freight Tracking → Settings → Appearance → Theme color. It applies to the quote form, tracking form and customer portal. You can override it for one instance with [consignly_quote_form color="#e8590c"], or with the Color panel when using the blocks.

Can I send emails from my company address?

Yes. Set Sender name and Sender email under Freight Tracking → Settings → Emails. For reliable delivery, your mail server or SMTP plugin must be authorised to send for that domain (SPF and DKIM). Some SMTP plugins force their own sender address and will override this setting. Customers who reply to one of the plugin emails reach your sender email, or your notification email if no sender is set.

The quote form says my session expired.

The form fetches a fresh security token when the page loads, so cached pages keep working. The message can still appear if JavaScript is blocked on a cached page older than about 12 hours: exclude that page from caching or shorten the cache lifetime.

I am behind a proxy or CDN and rate limiting blocks everyone.

Behind a reverse proxy on a private network this is handled automatically. If your proxy or CDN connects from a public address (for example Cloudflare), use the consignly_client_ip filter to return the real visitor IP.

How is the estimate calculated?

The built-in formula is: base price + (price per kg × total weight), configured per service under Freight Tracking → Settings → Services. It is only an indication; your team still confirms a final quote.

Can I customise the form fields or the estimate formula?

The free plugin ships a fixed set of fields and a simple formula. Both are built on extension points, so add-ons and custom code can change them (see the next question).

Do import and export adapt to my setup?

Yes. The quote export has a column for every field on your current quote form. The shipment import page, the downloadable template and the import itself all use one column list and your current statuses and services, so they always agree. Add-ons can add shipment columns with the consignly_shipment_csv_columns filter.

What hooks are available for developers?

Filters: consignly_quote_form_schema (steps and fields, including conditional logic), consignly_calculate_estimate, consignly_estimate_engine, consignly_form_manager, consignly_field_html, consignly_quote_prefill, consignly_statuses, consignly_services, consignly_cargo_types, consignly_estimate, consignly_email_headers, consignly_shipment_csv_columns, consignly_export_shipment_row, consignly_require_payment, consignly_portal_user_email, consignly_generate_tracking_number, consignly_client_ip, consignly_manage_capability.

Actions: consignly_loaded, consignly_quote_created, consignly_quote_updated, consignly_shipment_saved, consignly_shipment_status_changed, consignly_import_shipment_row, consignly_quote_offer_sent, consignly_quote_accepted, consignly_quote_declined, consignly_payment_confirmed, consignly_quote_response_extra.

Add-ons can check the CONSIGNLY_INTEGRATION_API constant to confirm they are compatible.
